title: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between November 7, 2025, and December 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NYSE, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Low implied volatility and resilient U.S. equity performance underpin the 85.5% market-implied probability that no NYSE marketwide circuit breaker will trigger before 2027.** The CBOE VIX has fallen to 14.1–14.5 in late August 2026, its lowest levels of the year, reflecting reduced hedging demand and contained near-term risk. Solid GDP growth, a balanced labor market with unemployment near 4.2%, and steady corporate earnings have supported S&P 500 levels above 7,600 amid elevated but stable PCE inflation around 3.7%. The Federal Reserve under Chair Warsh has maintained the federal funds target at 3.50–3.75%, with futures pricing only modest tightening odds. While September and October often see seasonal VIX rises, current readings leave ample room for normalization without reaching the 7% S&P 500 threshold that would activate Level 1 breakers. Key near-term catalysts include the September FOMC meeting and upcoming employment and inflation releases.
